title: Tidy a name
prompt:
A form lets people type their name carelessly, with extra spaces and odd capitals. Write a function `tidy_name(raw)` that returns the name with no spaces at the start or end, exactly one space between words, and each word starting with a capital letter followed by small letters.

For example, `tidy_name("  aNNa   maRIa ")` returns `"Anna Maria"`.
hints: `split()` with no argument ignores extra whitespace and returns a list of words.
`" ".join(words)` glues the words back together with one space.

title: Mail domain
prompt:
Read one email address from input. It may have spaces around it, so remove them first.

If the address contains an `@`, print everything after the `@`. If not, print `invalid`.

For example, the input `  mia@example.com ` gives `example.com`.
starter:
address = input()
# remove the spaces, find the @, print the part after it
hints: `strip()` removes spaces at both ends of a string and returns a new string, so store it.
`find("@")` returns the index of the `@`, or `-1` when it is missing.
The domain starts one place after the `@`: `address[at + 1:]`.
